cells.old: COMPOSITE KEY - position breakdown. Pattern ^[A-Z]{1,4}[0-9]+$. Numero = Prefix (NIE010) immediately followed by Sequence number (NIE011), with NO spaces and NO hyphens (the annex says so expressly). Sub-field 1 = the DIAN-authorised alphabetic prefix; sub-field 2 = the numeric consecutive. PERSISTENCE: unique per employee for the life of the range; it is input [1] to the CUNE, so it can never be re-issued after transmission.

cells.old: SOURCE CONFLICT. The annex percentages for codes 4, 5, 6 and 7 embed a 75% Sunday / public-holiday surcharge. Law 2101 of 2021 and Law 2466 of 2025 raise that surcharge to 80% from 1 July 2025 and to 90% from 1 JULY 2026, so from that date the statutory rate diverges from the printed annex value. The annex is still at version 1.0 and DIAN has not reissued table 5.5.5. This specification carries the annex values in @Porcentaje; the rate table is maintained as a configuration table, and the switch to the statutory value is made only on a written DIAN position.
cells.new: SOURCE CONFLICT. The annex percentages for codes 4, 5, 6 and 7 embed a 75% Sunday / public-holiday surcharge. Law 2466 of 2025 art. 14 (CST art. 179) raises that surcharge to 80% from 1 July 2025 and to 90% from 1 JULY 2026, so from that date the statutory rate diverges from the printed annex value. The annex is still at version 1.0 and DIAN has not reissued table 5.5.5. This specification carries the annex values in @Porcentaje; the rate table is maintained as a configuration table, and the switch to the statutory value is made only on a written DIAN position.

cells.old: Concatenate the DIAN-authorised Prefix (NIE010) with the next unused Sequence number (NIE011), with no separator. Persist the last-used consecutive per prefix range in a transactional store, and increment it BEFORE transmission, never after, so that a failed transmission does not leave a reusable number. Global rule 90 permits a given number only once per employee.
cells.new: Concatenate the issuer-chosen Prefix (NIE010) with the next unused Sequence number (NIE011), the consecutive also being assigned by the issuer (Res. DIAN 000227 de 2025 art. 1.5.3.3.1 num. 5), with no separator. Persist the last-used consecutive per prefix range in a transactional store, and increment it BEFORE transmission, never after, so that a failed transmission does not leave a reusable number. Global rule 90 permits a given number only once per employee.

cells.old: A rejected document consumes its number. On re-transmission the replacement document must carry a NEW consecutive. Never re-send a rejected number.
cells.new: Precaution: treat a rejected document's number as consumed. Global rule 90 only blocks a number already 'procesado anteriormente' (annex p.182), and the annex does not say whether a number from a rejected document may be reused; to be safe, the replacement document carries a NEW consecutive and a rejected number is not re-sent.

cells.new: Emit one element per contiguous block of hours of a single type. Split a block that crosses 19:00 or midnight, because the applicable code changes. Populate quantity, percentage and amount for every block, plus start and end times where the time register carries them.
